description: The check's derivations are made only of advances that the test allowed, as the main parse's are (tested-rebuilt-derivations). The chosen a elides one T, so R is X Y T. Only the body over Y sounds y, so a's [X] must read X. The derivation of R that reads [X] as empty and body over X Y is not counted, not even by a library that rebuilds the check's derivations from completed spans. So R has one reading, and the check passes (engine §4, §7.7).
grammar:
%ambiguity-resolution late-elision elision-only
%elidable T
%rule text a | b
%rule a [X] body="y" [T]
%rule b [X] body="y" [T] [T]
%rule body X Y | Y
